intent: Every platform that ships the UI verification skill or the UX validator scores visual work with the same critique rubric, PASS threshold, and round cap.
outcome: The Critique Rubric is byte-identical in frontend-verify on all five platforms (both Antigravity roots) and in ux-validator on Claude, Codex, both Antigravity roots, and OpenCode; it carries the harsh-reviewer stance, the seven-key score line, PASS only at 8 or more, and the 3-round cap that never ends in a claimed PASS. Each copy scores no-capture runs from the oracle reports with motion and design_system as n/a, and ux-validator no longer forbids numeric scores.

assertions.needle: Be a harsh reviewer, not a proud author: score only what the evidence shows, never what the code intended.
scores: hierarchy=N phone_360=N spacing=N states=N motion=N design_system=N a11y=N min=N
Verdict: PASS only when every scored key is 8 or more and no blocker shows;
The loop runs at most 3 rounds, and one that ends with any key below 8 reports the remaining gaps with WARN or FAIL and never claims PASS.
`motion` and `design_system` have no pixel evidence and are reported as `n/a`, never as a number; the verdict applies to the scored keys.
